DER portfolio scaling shows a nonmonotonic coordinated load reduction response, strongest at 20% penetration and decreasing at higher levels. On the 123 bus system, NTR reduces losses by 19.3%, while CVR reduces voltage dependent load energy by 2.3 to 2.4%. Under loading stress, SDN becomes infeasible at 120% loading, whereas CEDNTR remains feasible. Overall, the results demonstrate complementary, operating condition dependent benefits shaped by load composition, DER portfolio scaling, feeder topology, voltage margins, and source constraints, highlighting the value of joint optimization.

title: On the convexification of a bilinearly constrained set with a common variable
summary: We study the convexification of sets defined by box constraints and bilinear inequality constraints in which all bilinear terms share a common variable. For this structured class of nonconvex sets, we provide a complete characterization of the extreme points of the convex hull and derive an explicit description of all facet-defining inequalities, thereby obtaining a full polyhedral description of the convex hull. In addition, we develop a polynomial-time separation algorithm for the facet-defining inequalities and illustrate its effectiveness through examples. These results offer both structural insight into the geometry of the convex hull and algorithmic tools for identifying violated inequalities.

title: Safety-Critical Quadrotor Navigation Using Fourth-Order Control Barrier Functions with Full Nonlinear Quadrotor Dynamics
summary: Safety-critical quadrotor navigation in cluttered environments typically relies on hierarchical architectures in which a high-level safety filter modifies position references that are then tracked by a separate attitude controller. However, this separation can create a mismatch between translational safety objectives and attitude evolution. To address this gap, we propose a safety controller based on fourth-order control barrier functions (CBFs) that explicitly incorporates the full nonlinear quadrotor dynamics, including attitude dynamics and torque-level actuation. Furthermore, we apply the integral high-order CBF technique to resolve the mixed-relative degree issue in the derived constraint formulation. The resulting formulation enforces obstacle-avoidance constraints while optimizing control torques, granting the safety layer direct authority over attitude behavior and eliminating the hierarchical disconnect inherent in reference-tracking safety filters. We validate the approaches in both high-fidelity simulation and real-world flight experiments, demonstrating reliable constraint satisfaction and successful obstacle avoidance. These results suggest that torque-level high-order CBFs provide a practical pathway to provably safer quadrotor navigation under full rigid-body dynamics.

title: Reduced-Order Backstepping Control of Nonlinear Mechanical Systems with Input Delay via Galerkin Projection
comment: Accepted for presentation at the 65th IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC 2026)
summary: This paper addresses trajectory tracking for a class of nonlinear mechanical systems with input delay. The delayed actuator channel is represented as an equivalent transport partial differential equation, thereby transforming the original delayed system into a coupled plant-channel representation. A finite-dimensional approximation of the delay channel is then constructed through Galerkin projection, resulting in an explicit ODE model of the delayed actuator dynamics. Using this reduced-order plant-channel model, a backstepping controller is developed, and Lyapunov analysis establishes uniform exponential stability of the nominal tracking error dynamics for the reduced-order Galerkin model. To enhance practical implementation, a command-filtered version is also introduced to avoid direct differentiation of virtual controls, for which a corresponding uniform ultimate boundedness result is obtained. Simulation studies are provided to validate the proposed design and illustrate the effectiveness of the method.

title: Regularity of the Price of Anarchy in Routing Games over the Multivariate Demand Space
summary: We study the price of anarchy (PoA) in nonatomic routing games as a function of the full vector of origin--destination demands. We show that the Beckmann value function is continuously differentiable on the positive demand cone, with gradient equal to the equilibrium origin--destination cost vector; hence the PoA is continuously differentiable on the regular demand region. We prove that the nondifferentiability set has Lebesgue measure zero and, when every edge cost is strictly increasing or constant, is covered by countably many codimension-one submanifolds. Under the same cost structure, all equilibrium objects are cellwise as smooth as the edge costs. For affine costs, the exceptional sets become finite unions of lower-dimensional polyhedral cells linked by an exact scaling law, and the maximum of the PoA over a cell closure is attained on the cell boundary, generalizing the one-dimensional endpoint result. The theory is illustrated on the Sioux Falls benchmark network.

title: Who to Trust in Multi-Robot Systems: Joint Robot and Object Hypothesis Trust Inference via Neural-Symbolic Cross-Validation
summary: Multi-robot systems (MRS) offer significant advantages over single-robot platforms by enabling information sharing and coordination for different tasks in complex environments. However, reliable cooperation critically depends on inferring trust over both information sources and their reported hypotheses, particularly under partial observability and potential adversarial interference. Existing approaches frequently depend on pre-established trust relationships or side-channel information, which may not be available or reliable in realistic MRS deployments. This work introduces NeST-Bayes, a neural-symbolic framework that jointly infers robot and hypothesis trust using only inter-robot observation consistency, without requiring preassigned robot trust, reputation information, or side-channel identity signals. NeST-Bayes infers instantaneous trust evidence scores for robots and object hypotheses by reasoning over ego-centric relational graphs constructed from cross-robot observation consistency. These evidence scores are accumulated over time through Bayesian updates of Beta-distributed trust beliefs to maintain temporally consistent trust estimates. Extensive evaluations show that NeST-Bayes achieves the highest mean object precision and robot recall across all benchmark settings, and the highest robot precision and object recall in most settings, compared to trust-based methods. Under aggressive optimized attacks, it achieves 98.8\% robot precision with 93.8\% recall and 98.3\% object precision with 95.4\% recall. In an occlusion-rich Webots warehouse, it maintains 92.5\% robot precision with 92.0\% recall and 97.3\% object precision with 85.0\% recall. These results demonstrate joint improvements in the reliability and coverage of retained information.

title: Safety-Aware Dimension Selection for Reduced-Order Model Predictive Control
summary: Model reduction can substantially reduce the computational burden of model predictive control (MPC) for high-dimensional systems, but a reduced dimension chosen for performance may be insufficient for safety-critical operation. This paper introduces a safety-aware dimension-selection framework in which the prediction model adapts to the order of the model required to maintain a certified finite-horizon safety condition. Dynamic active subspaces provide a performance-oriented ordering of reduced coordinates, while finite-horizon error bounds robustly enforce discrete-time control barrier function constraints. The controller selects the smallest prediction order for which the resulting safety-critical MPC problem remains feasible. We establish full-order horizon safety, recursive feasibility, and closed-loop invariance of the safe set under the proposed reduced-order formulation. The proposed approach therefore adapts the prediction complexity to safety requirements, avoiding unnecessary high-dimensional prediction during benign operation.

title: Well-Posedness and Strong Convergence of Infinite-Dimensional Port-Hamiltonian Primal-Dual Gradient Dynamics
summary: We establish a functional-analytic framework that justifies the LaSalle convergence argument outlined in [van der Schaft, 2026] on port-Hamiltonian primal-dual gradient dynamics for finite-horizon optimal control of linear systems. In addition to strict convexity of the running cost as in \cite{vanderSchaft2026PDGJuly}, our analysis requires global Lipschitz continuity of the cost gradient. This ensures that the nonlinear gradient operator is well-defined and Lipschitz on the entire underlying space. We establish global well-posedness of the optimizer dynamics: every initial value determines a unique global mild solution, and the associated solution operators form a contraction semigroup. Similar to [Gernandtand Schaller, 2025], this is proved using tools from maximal monotone operator theory. Assuming existence of an optimal solution, we combine a dissipation inequality with an infinite-dimensional LaSalle invariance principle to prove strong convergence of every trajectory with a relatively compact positive orbit to the unique optimal state, control, and costate. Moreover, we present a sufficient condition for compactness through uniform control regularity and show that convergence holds for all initial states. Finally, we present an example with a strictly but not strongly convex running cost for which every mild solution converges strongly to the unique equilibrium, while no global exponential estimate uniformly over initial values can be obtained.

title: GG-Nav: Goal-oriented Grounding Chain-of-Thought Elicits Reasoning in Navigation Foundation Models
summary: Emerging strong Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have advanced navigation foundation models. However, these models still have unsatisfactory performance on goal-oriented navigation settings. In this paper, we first conduct a motivating study revealing that the key issue lies in the insufficient utilization of streaming observations and imprecise target localization. To tackle these challenges, we propose GG-Nav, a simple yet effective navigation framework that learns a structured chain-of-thought (CoT) mechanism via supervised fine-tuning to explicitly localize goal-relevant instances, accumulate grounding evidence, and support more reliable decision-making. Specifically, the structured CoT is designed with two key stages: (i) Observation-to-Evidence, which reasons over all intermediate frames between adjacent decision steps to retain useful goal-related evidence; and (ii) Evidence-to-Decision, which integrates the current observation with accumulated evidence to ground the target and support the generation of navigation actions or clarification questions. Extensive experiments show that GG-Nav outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in terms of success rates on the HM3D ObjectNav, VL-LN, and CoIN benchmarks by 3.1%, 16.6%, and 5.3%, respectively. Ablation studies further show that accumulating evidence from intermediate observations reduces evidence-missing failures by 11.6%, while explicit grounding reduces stopping errors by 49.4%. We also deploy GG-Nav on a Unitree Go2 robot, demonstrating its zero-shot generalization capability in unseen real-world environments.

title: Stabilizing Low-Stiffness Soft Robots at Unstable Equilibria: A Model-Based Optimal Control Approach
summary: Continuum soft robots are highly nonlinear and underactuated systems, which makes stabilizing them around unstable equilibrium points difficult. This challenge becomes even greater in low stiffness regimes, where gravitational forces dominate elastic forces. In this letter, we explore whether optimal control can address these challenges using a computa- tionally efficient method suitable for real time use. We propose a nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) approach based on Differential Dynamic Programming (DDP), combined with an accurate reduced order Variable Strain model with analytical derivatives. This results in an efficient control framework for addressing the stabilization problem. Tested on a soft inverted pendulum and other hybrid soft rigid systems, the method outperforms traditional controllers, stabilizes more challenging configurations, and operates reliably at real time speeds (50 150 Hz), demonstrating both effectiveness and practical feasibility in experimental settings.

title: On the Complexity of Finding Stationary Points of p-th Order Hölder Smooth Functions in One Dimension
summary: We study the query complexity of finding an an $\varepsilon$-stationary points of a one-dimensional non-convex function whose $p$-th derivative is $β_p$-Hölder continuous. We determine the optimal complexity for deterministic and randomized algorithms and for oracles that return only derivatives, only function values, or full local information. Randomness provably helps when only derivatives are available, function values help in all cases, and higher-order derivatives never do. Together with known results in higher dimensions, this shows how these benefits depend on the dimension. Our deterministic lower bound also implies that the optimal accuracy exponents of objective-function-free adaptive regularization of order $p$ (OFFAR$p$) in every dimension $d\ge1$ and of deterministic gradient-only trapping in dimension $d=2$.

title: Before We Act: Learning Action-Conditioned Team-Response Beliefs for Decentralized Multi-Robot Manipulation
summary: In multi-robot manipulation, an action's value depends on how teammates respond. We present \method{} (Cooperative Action--Response Belief Estimation), a framework for learning \emph{team-response beliefs} from local history. A predictive belief encoder represents the interaction and conditions a nominal action. Matched reactive and replay continuations separate each candidate's direct advantage from the utility contributed by teammate adaptation. A candidate-conditioned readout learns this response distribution alongside total advantage, and calibrated selection chooses an alternative or retains the nominal action. Our analysis characterizes when response changes the preferred action and how prediction and source errors limit the recoverable gain. With the representation, proposals, and data fixed, explicit response supervision improves candidate ranking and reduces selection regret relative to learning the same information through branch utilities. The benefit is concentrated in decisions where teammate adaptation changes the preferred action. Across RoboFactory, the MARS Control Track, and physical collaboration tasks, CARE achieves the highest average success among the evaluated policies, combining a capable nominal policy with selective coordination adjustments. Together, these results show that CARE turns predictions of teammate adaptation into effective decentralized action selection. Project page: https://jeong-zju.github.io/care/.

title: Reach-Avoid Certificates for Contact-based Stochastic Hybrid Systems
summary: This work studies certified reach-avoid control of stochastic hybrid systems in which a stochastic differential equation governs continuous flow and a controlled stochastic kernel governs guard-triggered resets. The input appears only in the reset kernel, where it determines the post-jump distribution. Certificates for such systems have so far assumed spontaneous or controller-chosen jump times, a finite horizon, or discrete-time dynamics; we certify, over the infinite horizon, that the target is reached before the unsafe set with at least a prescribed probability. First, we introduce reach-avoid contact certificates, whose flow and jump conditions are imposed only on a sublevel corridor, and prove that any such certificate with a compatible reset policy meets the specification; a pointwise safety filter extends this guarantee from verification to control by constraining arbitrary nominal controllers. Next, we prove that executions are non-Zeno and bound the expected settling time and reset count. We frame certificate search as a linear program over any twice-differentiable dictionary followed by independent verification. We illustrate our approach via comparisons where the certified region is a subset covering 93.6\% of the ground truth and where our certificate-based safety filter reaches the goal while reducing collisions from 68 to zero across 200 episodes of a dribbling ball problem.

title: Multiplicative Gradient Method for Log-Homogeneous Optimization: A Unified Mirror-Descent Framework
summary:
Consider the problems of computing $\ell_p$-Lewis weights, Kelly portfolios, D-optimal designs, general equilibria in Fisher markets, and optimal error exponents for channel coding in information theory. All of them can be formulated as optimization problems over the probability simplex, but except for the last one, the associated objective functions are neither Lipschitz continuous nor smooth, rendering existing first-order optimization algorithms and their guarantees not directly applicable. Nevertheless, first-order algorithms for solving these problems do exist in the literature and, perhaps surprisingly, look very similar, even though their interpretations, derivations, and analyses mostly appear unrelated. In this paper, we develop a framework unifying these results that captures their common problem structure through log-homogeneity and a novel second-order condition on the objective function, and identifies their common algorithmic pattern as multiplicative gradient methods.
  The framework recovers known algorithms and their optimization error guarantees for computing Kelly portfolios, D-optimal designs, optimal error exponents for channel coding in classical communication, $\ell_p$-Lewis weights with $p < 2$, and general equilibria in Fisher markets. To illustrate the insights provided by the framework, we further show that multiplicative gradient methods yield state-of-the-art performance guarantees for computing $\ell_p$-Lewis weights with $p > 2$ and optimal error exponents in classical-quantum communication. Both results are novel to the best of our knowledge.

title: From Video to Vision: Learning Generalizable Humanoid Carrying from Human Motion
summary: Most existing approaches rely on video or motion-capture data for reinforcement learning (RL) training; however, all of these methods require an upper-level module to generate reference trajectories in real time. In object carrying tasks, the humanoid can only lift objects from designated locations along the reference trajectory, resulting in poor spatial generalization. Moreover, existing policies can only be evaluated inside a motion-capture studio. To address these limitations, we propose \textbf{MOVER}, a multi-stage, Teacher-Assistant-Student, RL training framework for humanoid object carrying. We first collect data from videos and employ GENMO and GMR to retarget the video data, combining this with data augmentation techniques to generalize the data across objects of varying shapes and sizes. In the \textbf{first stage}, building upon the DeepMimic \cite{peng2018deepmimic} motion-training framework, we train the humanoid to transport objects from specified locations along designated trajectories. In the \textbf{second stage}, we relax the tracking of the reference motion and adjust the reward so that the humanoid learns to transport objects from different positions. In the \textbf{third stage}, we apply a Dagger-PPO distillation method to distill away the proprioceptive position observations and reference joint position of the humanoid. This allows the deployed policy to operate without relying on global position information from a motion-capture system; instead, the humanoid can directly perceive the object's pose from its onboard RGB-D camera to complete the carrying task. We design a series of simulation experiments to compare the success rates across stages (Stages 1 vs. 2) and before versus after distillation. We further transfer the policy to a real humanoid, successfully transporting objects at varying positions in a motion-capture-free setting.

title: STATCOM-Based Flicker Mitigation in Electric Arc Furnace Systems Using DQ-PI and Lyapunov-Based Nonlinear Control
comment: 18 pages, plus a 7-page supplementary document. Compiled with pdfLaTeX
summary: Electric arc furnaces inject stochastic reactive-power swings that cause voltage flicker at the point of common coupling. This paper compares two STATCOM inner controllers for an 11~kV, 50~Hz furnace feeder: a split-frequency DQ-PI design and a Lyapunov-based nonlinear design whose integral state is retained in the storage function, giving global asymptotic stability of the nominal unsaturated current-error subsystem. Gains for both controllers were tuned by a frozen metaheuristic campaign and then evaluated over 600~s with an IEC~61000-4-15 digital flickermeter. A post-campaign audit showed that the stochastic arc realization used for the original comparison was periodic, so the two selected gain sets were frozen without retuning or reselection and evaluated on ten independent stochastic realizations that had been specified and archived before the STO-ENS validation campaign, together with a paired uncompensated case for each realization. Both controllers reduce the mean short-term flicker severity by about 62% relative to the STO-ENS uncompensated baseline, and no statistically detectable difference in mean flicker severity is found between them. They separate instead in realization sensitivity: the Lyapunov standard deviation across arcs is roughly one third that of DQ-PI. Controller ordering inferred from a single stochastic trajectory is therefore not a reliable measure of stochastic robustness, and ensemble validation is necessary.

title: Taming Nonconvexity with Epigraph Lifting
summary: We consider inverse problems regularized by a trained neural network with \emph{convex activations} and \emph{unrestricted weights}. The resulting optimization problem is generally nonconvex, and gradient-based methods may converge to poor local minima. We introduce a \emph{penalized epigraph lifting} of the network and show that the lifted problem admits a \emph{difference-of-convex (DC) decomposition}. For Lipschitz continuous activations, we establish \emph{finite exactness}: the original objective is recovered exactly at a finite and explicitly computable penalty threshold $\barρ$. Building on this structure, we propose \emph{H-DC} (Homotopic DC), a homotopic scheme that solves a sequence of DC subproblems with increasing $ρ$, warm-starting each level from the previous solution. Numerical experiments on synthetic problems, a manifold denoiser regularizer, and image inpainting with a learned Mumford--Shah regularizer show that H-DC consistently escapes poor local minima and reaches solutions with lower objective values than gradient-based methods from the same initialization.

title: Chunk-wise Model-based Policy Optimization
summary: Model-based reinforcement learning has shown superior sample efficiency by leveraging the learned latent dynamics either in the form of derivative-free planning/imagined rollout training or dynamics gradient-based policy updates. While these approaches achieve comparatively fast learning, they all suffer, to varying degrees, from issues of recurrent compounding errors, high inference-time latency, and instability in backward propagation through time (BPTT). In this work, we propose a model-based RL approach that uses the chunk world model as a differentiable training-time evaluator to optimize the chunk actor without recurrent model invocation. Through the collaborative chunk-wise prediction of the world model and policy, we can generate H-step hypothetical rollouts in a single forward pass and directly optimize value expansion, avoiding the costly and unstable BPTT. We evaluate our method on 19 challenging high-dimensional humanoid tasks from HumanoidBench and deploy our method to the real-world for quadruped bipedal walking. Project Website: https://song-wx.github.io/cmpo.github.io/

title: Filtering for Liveness: Recurrence via Backup Reachability Control Barrier Functions
summary: Liveness requires a dynamical system to repeatedly accomplish a desired objective over time. In this work, we consider a particular form of liveness known as recurrence, which requires the closed-loop trajectory to regularly revisit a prescribed set, with no more than a specified amount of time between visits. Inspired by the control barrier function (CBF) safety-filter paradigm, we develop a controller-filtering framework that makes adjustments to a nominal controller only when necessary to guarantee recurrence. Unlike conventional CBF methods, which enforce set forward invariance, our framework allows the trajectory to leave the set while guaranteeing its timely return. To achieve this, our framework combines two components: a backup reachability CBF that preserves the ability to return to the prescribed set within the allowable time, and a timing-based mechanism that invokes a reaching controller only when the nominal behavior would otherwise fail to meet the return-time requirement. The resulting framework guarantees recurrence while preserving the nominal behavior when possible, enabling control objectives that require temporary excursions from the set, such as traversal between disjoint regions. Our method is successfully utilized in a drone racing example with a recurrence constraint on beacon visibility.

title: Towards learning-enhanced solvers for multi-parametric optimization
comment: 8 pages, 3 figures, to be published in the proceedings of the 65th IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (2026)
summary:
Neural networks (NNs) have been employed in various ways to accelerate the solution of multi-parametric optimization problems (OPs), which prominently arise in model predictive control (MPC). Early approaches focused on approximating the parametric solution (e.g., the optimal control law) directly by NNs. More recently, learning-based techniques have been used to emulate or enhance solver iterations. For the direct approximation of the parametric solution, it has been demonstrated that exploiting structural properties of the underlying OP facilitates the design of suitable NN architectures. In this paper, we show that structural analysis can also be leveraged to systematically integrate learning into classical optimization algorithms, thereby enhancing their performance.
  We formalize our concept for the case of multi-parametric quadratic programs (mpQPs), which frequently arise in linear-quadratic MPC, as a representative application. More precisely, we demonstrate that tailored NNs enable a parameter-dependent fine-tuning of the step sizes in a standard dual projected gradient scheme. The design of the NNs is guided by the observation that optimal step sizes, which permit obtaining the exact optimal solution in finitely many iterations, are piecewise constant functions over the parameter space (e.g., the state space in MPC). We establish key theoretical properties of the proposed approach and illustrate its effectiveness in a numerical case study.

title: In View or Out of View? A Vision-Aware Filter that Infers and Reacts to the Human's Field of View
summary: During human-robot interaction, sight plays an important role. When the human sees a robot, they can observe the robot's actions and better predict the robot's future behaviors. Conversely, when the human cannot see the robot, they become uncertain about the robot's intent and plans. In this paper, we focus on the human's field of view. Existing human-aware planners either ignore this field of view and assume the human can observe the entire scene, or intentionally design their interactions so the robot is always visible to the human. By contrast, we enable robots to infer what the human has and has not seen during interaction, i.e., the human's field of view. We then apply this estimate as a vision-aware filter on the robot's actions. Given a nominal robot policy and a model of the interaction, we roll out the policy over a short horizon to see how the robot's state updates. We then reweight the actions based on how those actions impact the robot's predicted visibility: higher weights are assigned to actions that bring the robot into (or away from) the human's line of sight. In practice, our framework provides an online estimation and filtering process that repeatedly updates its understanding of the human's field of view and then locally perturbs robot actions based on the human's vision. We evaluate our vision-aware filter on robots that assist humans in collaborative cooking and coordinate with them in driving environments. Across simulations and a 12-participant user study, we find that our vision-aware filter changes both performance and preference: participants completed over three times as many subtasks with in-view assistance while cooking, and had fewer collisions with cars that purposely stayed out of their view while driving.

title: Direct Electromechanical Actuation of the Shift Drum in Non-Synchronized Motorcycle Transmissions: From Actuator Sizing and Electronics Design to Closed-Loop Position Control
comment: Original German title (2019): Entwickeln eines automatisierten Schaltgetriebes fuer Motorraeder. Diploma thesis, Westsaechsische Hochschule Zwickau, 2019; revised English edition 2026. 73 pages, 30 figures, 15 tables. Firmware and shift time dataset: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23002655)
summary: This thesis presents the direct electromechanical actuation of the shift drum in a non-synchronized motorcycle transmission. A DC motor drives the shift drum through a self-locking worm gear, so the entire foot shift mechanism is eliminated. As a reference, 84 manual gear changes of a large-displacement series-production motorcycle were measured on a chassis dynamometer; the mean shift time is 80 ms for upshifts and 92 ms for downshifts. The system design covers the complete chain from the mechanics to the software. The actuator motor is sized from inertia, friction and gear ratio. A dedicated shift controller is developed with supply filtering, signal conditioning for the position sensor and the incremental encoder, an H-bridge motor driver and a custom circuit board based on a SAMD21 microcontroller. The embedded firmware implements position control of the shift drum with a proportional controller, without inner speed or current loops. On a gearbox test rig, a gear change is completed in less than 80 ms without overshoot in a single measurement, below the mean of the manual reference shifts. The analysis reveals a trade-off in the choice of the worm gear ratio: at a ratio of 30, about 93% of the motor torque is needed to accelerate the motor shaft and the worm. A ratio of about 8 halves the required torque, but the worm gear then loses its self-locking. The measured shift times are published as an open dataset.

title: Preconditioned Latent Variable Proximal Point Method for Optimal Control Problems with Control Constraints
summary: The latent variable proximal point (LVPP) method solves optimization problems in function spaces with pointwise constraints by a sequence of smooth subproblems whose iterates are strictly feasible. We apply it to linear-quadratic elliptic optimal control problems. Control and observation are distributed but may be restricted to subdomains. We prove that the LVPP subproblems are well posed in appropriate function spaces, that the iteration converges for every sequence of proximity parameters with divergent sum, and that it delivers the Lagrange multiplier of the constraint as a by-product. We interpret the Newton step for the LVPP subproblem as a linear-quadratic optimal control problem with a spatially varying control cost, and we show that Newton's method converges locally quadratically. The Newton systems are solved by the minimal residual method with a block-diagonal preconditioner. We prove that the spectrum of the Newton operator with respect to the inner product defined by the preconditioner is bounded independently of the proximity parameter, the iterate, the mesh and the observation and control domains. The results are combined into a complete algorithm, and tested in numerical experiments.

title: Remembering What Matters for Long-Horizon Robotic World Models
summary: Autoregressive robot video world models based on discrete visual tokens remain unreliable over long rollout horizons. Retaining the entire generated history does not necessarily improve prediction quality. We investigate a possible memory-role conflict in Full Context decoding: persistent scene information, recent visual-action states, and stale generated history compete for attention despite their different predictive roles. This perspective motivates ReCAP (Receding Context with Anchor Preservation), a training-free context-scheduling method for long-horizon robot video world models. ReCAP keeps the pretrained tokenizer, world model, and visual decoder frozen. It preserves the initial scene anchor and a contiguous window of recent complete visual-action blocks while evicting older generated history. The schedule preserves within-block structure and temporal order, requires no additional modules or parameter updates, and bounds active-context growth independently of rollout length. We evaluate ReCAP on RT-1, BridgeV2, LIBERO-90, and CALVIN using frozen autoregressive world models. Across evaluated environments and horizons, ReCAP improves visual fidelity, action-conditioned consistency, and robot structure preservation relative to Full Context. On BridgeV2, it reduces LPIPS by 63.3%. In the system benchmark at H=64, it reduces the logical KV footprint by 73.3% and p50 latency by 6.51%. Attention analyses show increased attention to retained recent states, while history interventions associate larger amounts of stale context with higher prediction error. These observations are consistent with the memory-role-conflict hypothesis, although they do not isolate it from context-length and position-handling effects. Our results support inference-time context scheduling as a practical approach to improving long-horizon robot video prediction and computational efficiency without retraining.

title: Input-Constrained Active Disturbance Rejection Control for AUVs
summary: This paper addresses the control of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) operating in dynamic environments, where wave-induced forces, modelling errors, and actuator limitations make reliable control challenging. Active disturbance rejection control (ADRC), together with an extended state observer (ESO), estimates lumped uncertainties online, simplifying control design using nominal models. However, existing stability analyses typically assume bounded control inputs and derivatives, which are difficult to guarantee under unknown disturbances and measurement noise. To bridge this theory--practice gap, this paper introduces an ADRC framework with active input saturation and post-saturation low-pass filtering. The saturation constrains the control magnitude, while the filter regularizes the saturated signal to ensure bounded input-rate variations. By explicitly enforcing these conditions, the proposed system guarantees semi-global practical asymptotic stability. High-fidelity simulations and experiments on an underwater robotic platform demonstrate robust control performance under severe environmental disturbances and actuator constraints. A supplementary video is available at https://youtu.be/AEFlZ69Yg00.

title: Globally Convergent Block Coordinate Descent Algorithms for Semi-Nonnegative Independent Component Analysis
summary: We propose a subgradient-based block coordinate descent (BCD-SubG) framework for nonconvex optimization over products of probability simplices and a closed feasible set, motivated by semi-nonnegative independent component analysis (Semi-NNICA). Elementary column transformations are used to preserve simplex feasibility, while first-order information guides block and pair selection. We establish the global convergence of BCD-SubG using a constrained Lojasiewicz inequality; additional eventual-interiority conditions yield stationary limits and convergence rates. We then specialize BCD-SubG to the direct-fit and indirect-fit Semi-NNICA models and derive explicit updates that ensure global convergence without further assumptions. For both models, eventual interiority also yields stationary limits and convergence-rate estimates. Experiments on synthetic mixtures and simulated magnetic resonance spectroscopy data show generally lower recovery errors and shorter wall-clock times than the tested Semi-NNICA baselines. Joint diagonalization experiments further demonstrate lower final objective values.

title: PC7 Model: Dynamics of Expanding and Contracting Soft Robots using Piece-wise Constant 7D Deformation Based on Similarity Transformation Group
summary: This paper proposes a novel soft robot model named piece-wise constant 7D deformation (PC7) model that can represent expanding and contracting deformation of, for example, artificial muscle actuator. In the proposed model, we newly define the 7D deformation vector based on SIM(3) - 3D similarity transformation group - whereas a 6D deformation vector was defined for Cosserat rod based on SE(3) - the special Euclid group - in the piece-wise constant strain (PCS) model proposed in the previous study. The additional dimension of the 7D deformation vector represents expanding and contracting deformation, which comes from the scaling parameter in SIM(3). Common mathematical properties between SE(3) and SIM(3) allow us to directly extend the kinematics and dynamics of the PCS model to those of the PC7 model. In particular, we derive the dynamical equation of the PC7 model based on Euler-Poincare equation in a mathematically precise manner. We validate the proposed model through dynamical simulations assuming a thin cylinder structure or McKibben-type artificial muscle actuator.

title: Multi-Day Stochastic Dispatch for Power Systems With Long-Duration Storage Using Diffusion-Generated Weather Forecasts
summary: As power systems shift toward high shares of wind and solar, long-duration storage becomes pivotal for balancing multi-day deficits and surpluses of uncertain supply and demand. Current dispatch strategies for long-duration storage either assign a fixed value to stored energy or extend the modeled horizon using a single forecast. Stochastic system dispatch with a multi-day horizon for long-duration storage remains unexplored, and existing stochastic dispatch only considers day-ahead uncertainty or Markovian uncertainty beyond one week of perfect foresight. Therefore, we benchmark stochastic multi-day dispatch against deterministic alternatives in a rolling-horizon setup. To emulate probabilistic multi-day forecasts, we combine diffusion with a semi-Markov model of weather regimes and a logistic growth model for meteorological forecast errors. At high renewable shares, stochastic operation reduces thermal backup generation and consistently eliminates loss of load. The benefits decrease with smaller shares of renewables, less long-duration storage, or higher forecast skill. Overall, our results suggest that systems with high shares of variable renewables can substantially benefit from probabilistic multi-day forecasts and stochastic dispatch.

title: On the Stability of Power Systems with AI Data Centers: A Multi-Equilibrium Switched DAE Framework
summary: The rapid growth of Artificial Intelligence (AI) data centers is introducing dynamic loads into power transmission systems as GPU clusters switch between computational phases with distinct power demands. These dynamics are naturally modeled by switched affine differential-algebraic equations (DAEs), where each mode induces a different equilibrium and consistency space. We study their stability using control and hybrid systems tools. Differential projectors derived from the quasi-Weierstrass form yield an equivalent hybrid representation, from which we characterize the $ω$-limit set and establish Lyapunov conditions for practical stability with an explicit $\mathcal{KL}$ bound accounting for switching-induced resets. For stochastic inference workloads, we use Foster--Lyapunov techniques to establish probabilistic uniform global recurrence under mode-dependent dwell times and transition probabilities. The framework is validated on the IEEE 39-bus transmission network with co-located AI data centers using high-fidelity electromagnetic transient simulations of deterministic training and stochastic inference workloads.

title: Flow-Support-Weighted Proposals for Test-Time Verified VLA Policies
comment: 35 pages, 5 figures, under review in AAAI 2027
summary: Test-time sampling promises to turn one action prediction into a set of distinct executable candidates that a verifier can choose among. Downstream fine-tuning works against that promise. A vision-language-action model trained to solve one task distribution concentrates its flow-matching decoder around the dominant demonstrated action, so repeated samples differ only marginally and the verifier receives many copies of one decision. We call this proposal contraction and identify it as a key constraint on test-time scaling: repeated samples can remain highly redundant as the candidate budget grows. Action Dynamic Sampling (ADS) alleviates the constraint on the proposal side, during training. At each training step, ADS integrates $K$ additional trajectories from the current policy under fresh base noise, scores each by the flow support along its path with a Hutchinson trace estimator, and corrects the policy's local action distribution toward this weighted set through a detached finite-set KL term. Training cost rises; deployment cost is unchanged. Across simulation and four physical-robot tasks, ADS raises proposal spread without the success penalty that Gaussian perturbation incurs, lifts oracle best-of-8 success on RoboCasa from 57.6% to 63.0%, improves fixed verifiers by 2.4 to 4.9 points in simulation, and raises TokenPB by up to 13.0 points on real-world manipulation.

title: A Collision-Aware Predictive Rerouting Framework for Connected and Automated Vehicles
summary: In this paper, we investigate the problem of mitigating non-recurrent congestion in urban transportation networks through predictive and adaptive routing for connected and automated vehicles (CAVs). We propose a collision-aware predictive rerouting framework that integrates microscopic SUMO simulation, DCRNN-based spatiotemporal traffic-state forecasting, collision-window lookahead, and multi-objective route scoring. The routing controller uses predicted congestion, live emission information, route-length penalties, and incident-window constraints to decide when CAVs deviate from their current routes. The completed simulation campaign across three urban network scenarios, five CAV penetration levels, three random seeds, and multiple benchmark rerouting strategies shows that the proposed full framework does not dominate all baselines in aggregate travel time, distance, or emissions. Instead, its principal advantage is operational stability: it maintains comparable network-level efficiency while substantially reducing rerouting frequency relative to active rerouting baselines. These results demonstrate both the promise and the tradeoffs of embedding graph-based prediction and collision awareness into real-time CAV rerouting, and they motivate further work on forecast calibration, uncertainty-aware prediction, and system-level fairness between CAV and non-CAV traffic.

title: Matching Full-Hessian Oracle Complexity for Nonconvex--Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization
summary:
We characterize the oracle complexity of finding first-order stationary points in smooth nonconvex--strongly-concave (NC--SC) minimax optimization when each query provides the full Hessian in addition to the function value and gradient. For $Φ(x)=\max_y f(x,y)$, assume that $f$ has an $L$-Lipschitz gradient, a $ρ$-Lipschitz Hessian, and is $μ$-strongly concave in $y$. Let $κ=L/μ$, let $Δ$ denote the initial value gap, and define $r=ρκ^{3/2}\varepsilon/L^2$.
  We establish matching deterministic upper bounds and randomized lower bounds, up to logarithmic factors and additive initialization costs. When the leading term dominates initialization, the resulting minimax complexity is \[ \widetildeΘ\!\left( \frac{ΔL}{\varepsilon^2}Ψ_κ(r) \right), \qquad Ψ_κ(r)= \begin{cases} r^{1/2}, & 0<r\le 1,\\ r^{2/7}, & 1<r<κ^{7/4},\\ \sqrtκ, & r\geκ^{7/4}. \end{cases} \] Despite the stronger oracle, the optimal complexity exhibits a nontrivial dependence on accuracy, conditioning, and Hessian smoothness. In particular, these regimes exhibit accuracy dependencies $\varepsilon^{-3/2}$, $\varepsilon^{-12/7}$, and $\varepsilon^{-2}$, respectively.
  The upper bounds combine second-order regularity estimates for a saddle Moreau envelope with certified accelerated reduced-dual solves and amortized warm starts. The lower bounds combine an all-derivative lift with a serial composition of private-handle constructions, using hard instances chosen independently of the algorithm's realized random seed. The resulting characterization quantifies improvements over the classical first-order benchmark under gradient smoothness alone and identifies the regime in which that benchmark is recovered.

title: ToF-Wheel Odometry: Navigating Degeneration of Localization With Limited Sensing Capabilities
comment: 9 pages, 4 figures, 5 tables. Accepted by IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L)
summary: Wheel odometry provides an efficient motion prior for ground robots but is prone to transient violations such as wheel slip or terrain-induced tilt. In filtering-based odometry, these violations frequently trigger divergence when they coincide with constrained geometric observability (e.g., featureless corridors). We address this challenge by proposing ToF-Wheel Odometry (TWO), a tightly-coupled filtering framework that integrates wheel kinematics with geometric constraints from Time-of-Flight (ToF) cameras. The primary contribution of this work is a degeneracy-aware, directional covariance-shaping strategy that replaces heuristic online covariance tuning with geometry-conditioned inflation. The core idea is to infer process noise from geometric corrections with a strict reliability check. We decompose the posterior-to-prior correction into a wheel-explainable subspace and an orthogonal remainder. The process covariance is anisotropically adjusted according to the observability of the ToF update: if the geometry is degenerate in non-kinematic directions, the remainder is suppressed as sensor noise; if the geometry is distinct, it is admitted as a valid kinematic violation. Additionally, we introduce an intra-frame feedback loop that retrospectively repairs the process covariance within the current frame to reduce structural lag during bursty disturbances. Extensive experiments on challenging scenarios demonstrate that TWO improves trajectory accuracy and robustness compared to static and adaptive Gaussian filtering, robustly navigating the trade-off between kinematic reliability and limited sensing capabilities.

title: Stability Transfer for Autonomous Systems via Higher-Order Taylor-Truncated Lyapunov Certificates
summary: We develop analytical sufficient conditions for certifying the local asymptotic stability of nonlinear autonomous systems based on Lyapunov functions derived from their finite-order Taylor polynomial approximations. This approach translates the stability analysis problem from the original nonlinear dynamics to a more computationally tractable polynomial domain. The derived conditions allow for the explicit calculation of a guaranteed inner approximation of the region of attraction ($\mathrm{ROA}$). We show how sum-of-squares (SOS) programming and grid search can be used to systematically search for polynomial Lyapunov functions that yield a large certified threshold radius and extract a certified invariant set inner approximation of the $\mathrm{ROA}$ of the nonpolynomial original system. The framework is then applied to a control tuning problem: finding reduced-effort Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) controllers that ensure that a given initial state of interest belongs to the certified $\mathrm{ROA}$ of the nonpolynomial closed loop system. The effectiveness of the overall methodology is demonstrated using a pendulum with nonlinear damping and a nonlinear control system.

title: Calibrated $α$-Barycenters for Multiobjective $f$-Divergence Optimization
comment: 51 pages, 38 figures, 8 tables, comments are welcome!
summary: Matching one distribution to many targets can require repeated evaluations of every target. CAL-$α$-MODM aggregates a nonlinear predictor into one barycenter, calibrates its residual derivatives, and checks steps against the original $f$-divergence objective. Under smoothness assumptions, calibration controls parameter-step model error without requiring targets to be close to the model. Exact-oracle stationarity and local convergence guarantees are established. At common matching, canonical geometry cancels the leading quadratic iteration error, giving cubic convergence with second-order calibration and sufficiently accurate inner solves. High-precision experiments support this prediction. Sensitivity-based initialization also accelerates preference continuation along regular stationary branches. On 300-target Jensen--Shannon problems, CAL-p2 achieves median paired speedups of $3.15\times$ over L-BFGS and $1.10\times$ over second-order Direct-TR, across 23/25 and 24/25 objective-comparable stationary pairs. The savings arise when cheaper predictor queries offset calibration overhead.

title: Load-Aware Quadruped Navigation with Online Contact-based Geometry Estimation
comment: 19 pages, 12 figures, 5 tables. Project website: https://qiii04.github.io/LOADNav/
summary: Navigating cluttered environments while carrying objects remains a challenging problem for quadruped robots. Compared with works that focused on load-aware locomotion adaptation to maintain gait stability, existing autonomous navigation systems generally ignore the influence of carried objects' geometries and use fixed footprint inflation, leading to overly conservative navigation. To fill this knowledge gap, we propose a two-phase load-aware navigation learning framework. In Phase 1, we train LOADNav, a load-aware navigation policy via reinforcement learning, enabling the robot to adapt its trajectory and clearance behavior according to the geometric size of the carried object. In Phase 2, we train CoGE, an online geometry predictor via imitation learning, which estimates unknown payload geometry from occasional contact events. We evaluate the framework in cluttered environments with loads of varying sizes and shapes. The results show that our navigation policy exhibits clear load-aware behaviors, and the online geometry predictor estimates object geometry from occasional contact events, refining its estimate and adapting the navigation behavior accordingly. Without requiring any prior knowledge of the payload, it narrows the gap to geometry-aware policies.

title: Constrained Grid-Forming Control for Photovoltaic Systems: A Control Barrier Function Approach
summary: This paper leverages control barrier functions (CBFs) to systematically account for constraints of voltage source converters (VSCs) and photovoltaic (PV) resources in grid-forming (GFM) control. The proposed control combines (unconstrained) dual-port GFM control with control barrier functions (CBFs) to ensure reliable and safe operation of a GFM PV system under grid faults, sudden changes in irradiance, and load perturbations. First, CBFs are used to encode physical and operational limits of the PV system, namely current and voltage limits at its ac and dc terminals. Then, CBFs are used to restrict the dynamics of dual-port GFM control to within the VSC and PV limits during both transient and steady states. To this end, a cost function is defined that encodes trade-offs between forming the ac voltage phase angle/frequency and voltage magnitude under constraints. Then, real-time optimization is used to make the least modification, as measured by the cost function, to the (unconstrained) dual-port GFM control state to remain within the safe set encoded by the CBFs. Finally, the performance of the developed constrained GFM control is evaluated through EMT simulations in MATLAB/Simulink.

title: Matching Complexity for Second-Order Stationary Point with Sample Reuse
summary: We consider stochastic nonconvex optimization with sample-wise Lipschitz gradients and Hessians, and reusable opaque sample handles. Gradient and complete-Hessian evaluations are charged separately, including both endpoints of a same-sample difference. For fixed positive problem parameters and in the high-dimensional worst case, we prove that the minimax total derivative-query complexity of finding an $(\varepsilon,γ)$-second-order stationary point is \begin{equation*} \widetildeΘ(\varepsilon^{-3}+γ^{-3}). \end{equation*} The upper bound combines curvature-first randomly signed negative-curvature steps with binary-ancestor derivative estimators; a truncated increment estimate charges predictable drift linearly and martingale motion quadratically. The curvature lower bound uses a deterministic smooth bounded-gradient chain, a radial barrier, and a random rotation. The new first-order lower bound is specifically robust to persistent sample reuse and to complete-Hessian access. It uses a slowly parameterized conservative sign chain, a third-order reverse stick-breaking localization inequality, and stateful relative-entropy accounting for reusable handles. Thus the total rate is near-optimally matched for every relation between $\varepsilon$ and $γ$.

title: StateSkill-Agent: An Effective and Efficient Embodied Agent via State-conditioned Skill
summary: In this work, we aim to develop an embodied MLLM agent that understands and solves embodied tasks by learning, abstracting, and reusing transferrable and generalizable behavioral patterns. To this end, we propose StateSkill, a new skill representation for embodied agents, which introduces the concept of "finite-state machines" into skill modeling for effective and efficient skill construction and learning. The core idea of StateSkill is to model embodied interaction experiences as a finite-state machine, where a skill is organized around a set of task-progress states, state transitions, and state-conditioned guidance, enabling embodied agents to dynamically adjust their skills as the task progresses while keeping skill contexts compact and stage-relevant. We further develop StateSkill-Evolve, an experience-driven evolution mechanism that iteratively refines StateSkill through retrospective analysis of new successful and failed state-guided trajectories. Upon this, we introduce StateGRPO, which integrates StateSkill evolution and model optimization via state-conditioned GRPO into a unified iterative learning loop, enabling state-conditioned skills and model capabilities to co-evolve and reinforce each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed methods and trained model (i.e., StateSkill-Agent) across various embodied tasks.

title: Service-Aware Hosting Capacity Assessment of Edge Data Centers with Workload Flexibility
summary: The growing demand for edge computing, content delivery, and AI services is driving the interconnection of edge data centers (DCs) with distribution networks. Before interconnection, utilities evaluate how much DC capacity can be accommodated without violating feeder current and voltage limits. Fixed peak load representations can overlook service dependent demand patterns, cooling related facility demand, and delay tolerant computing tasks. This paper develops a hosting capacity (HC) assessment model for edge DCs with shiftable workload scheduling. Three representative types are considered: mobile edge computing (MEC), content delivery network (CDN), and AI DCs. Facility demand is modeled by combining fixed base demand, service driven demand, prescribed cooling-overhead coefficient, and a shiftable workload component. Workload execution is optimized under arrival causality, maximum delay, daily energy balance constraints, and the resulting active and reactive loads are embedded in a distribution power flow model. Compared with the baseline without load shifting, the maximum bus level HC gain on the IEEE 33-bus system reaches 4.46% for MEC DCs and 9.89% for AI DCs, while CDN case shows negligible gain under the assumed cache management windows.

title: A Composite Bayesian Risk--Distributionally Robust Optimization Model for Stochastic Programming with Elliptical Distribution Ambiguity
summary: We study a stochastic optimization problem in which the random vector follows a semiparametric elliptical distribution with unknown location and shape parameters and an unspecified radial distribution. Assuming that the decision maker only has access to samples of the random vector, we develop a framework to jointly address parameter uncertainty and distributional ambiguity arising from this composite structure. To update the posterior distribution of the parameters, a key challenge is that the density of an elliptical distribution depends on the unknown radial distribution, and hence conventional likelihood-based Bayesian inference is infeasible. To overcome this challenge, we propose a novel estimating-equation-based Gibbs inference framework that updates posterior distributions of model parameters solely through estimating equations. For elliptical distributions, we construct a pair of estimating equations for the location and shape parameters that are invariant to the radial component, which enables posterior learning without specifying the density. For the distributional uncertainty, we construct an ambiguity set for the radial distribution by transforming observed samples into pseudo-samples of the radial variable. Combining the above components, we formulate a composite Bayesian risk--distributionally robust optimization model, in which the inner problem captures worst-case radial distributions within the ambiguity set, and the outer problem evaluates the decision risk induced by the parameter uncertainty through a user-specified risk measure. We further develop a cutting-plane algorithm to solve the resulting optimization problem. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach provides substantial performance improvements over benchmark methods, including sample average approximation and distributionally robust optimization.

title: AnyRank: Reliable Anytime Policy Ranking via Sequential Testing
summary: Due to the high cost of hardware experiments, robot policies are predominantly evaluated by comparing their empirical performance on a limited number of hardware trials. However, finite-sample statistical uncertainty can lead to erroneous conclusions, especially when ranking multiple policies using a fixed batch of evaluation data. We propose AnyRank: a sequential method for multi-policy ranking that (i) adaptively allocates trials to hard-to-separate policies, (ii) provides (partial) rankings at any stopping time while bounding the probability of an incorrect ranking, and (iii) optionally exploits prior information to prioritize hardware evaluations more efficiently. This prior information could be informed from expert intuition, a small set of held-out hardware evaluations, or from policy rollouts in a simulator or an action-conditioned video world model. Notably, the prior can be imperfect; while a strong prior can provide efficiency gains on hardware, any inaccuracies in prior policy rankings do not invalidate the statistical assurances of AnyRank. We achieve the aforementioned properties through novel theoretical contributions that combine sequential testing with multiple-hypothesis graphical testing approaches. Experiments in simulation and real-world policy evaluation benchmarks show that AnyRank requires up to 50% fewer hardware evaluations compared to existing statistically rigorous approaches, while guarding against the incorrect rankings produced by heuristic methods used by state-of-the-art benchmarks.

title: A Programming, Robotics and Automatic Control Intervention for Secondary Education Students in Sweden and Italy
comment: This paper has 40 pages and 10 figures. Partial results have been presented at NPCW26 in Denmark and are available at https://npcw2026.compute.dtu.dk/Yamashita_npcw2026.pdf
summary: This study evaluates the AutoSTEM workshop, an intervention for secondary education that combines a serious game with PID-controlled hardware. Seven workshops were conducted across Sweden and Italy. The six Swedish workshops adopted an explicitly SDT-informed facilitation framework, while the Italian workshop followed the existing educational robotics format without a formally defined SDT facilitation protocol. Self-reports, an objective knowledge quiz, and qualitative responses were analysed using multiple site-adjusted statistical approaches. Technical-specific self-efficacy increased substantially in both conditions, with large effect sizes, while objective knowledge showed only modest, non-significant gains. No significant site-adjusted differences were found between SDT and control conditions for the primary outcomes. Perceived engagement was higher in the control condition, although this finding should be interpreted cautiously. The objective knowledge composite remained positive but non-significant across sensitivity analyses. Female participants reported smaller PID self-efficacy gains than males. Qualitative findings supported evidence of PID learning while identifying technical and pacing barriers. Overall, the results suggest that the technology-rich intervention supports competence development, regardless of SDT-informed facilitation.

title: Extragradient and Past Extragradient Methods for $(L_0,L_1)$-Lipschitz Variational Inequalities
summary: Variational inequalities (VIs) capture a broad class of optimization problems central to modern machine learning, including min-max optimization and equilibrium computation in multiplayer games. Traditionally, algorithms for solving VIs, such as Extragradient (EG) and Past Extragradient (PEG), have been analyzed under the standard $L$-Lipschitz assumption. However, this condition is often overly restrictive, and recent works have instead turned to the more relaxed $(L_0,L_1)$-Lipschitz setting. Existing guarantees for $(L_0,L_1)$-Lipschitz VIs require a quasi-sharpness condition [Vankov et al., 2024], while monotone guarantees for EG cover only unconstrained root finding [Choudhury and Loizou, 2025]. In this work, we provide the first convergence guarantees for EG and PEG for monotone $(L_0,L_1)$-Lipschitz VIs. We also improve upon prior convergence guarantees for strongly monotone VIs by supporting larger stepsizes in the constrained setting and eliminating exponential dependence on the initial distance from the solution for convergence rates in the unconstrained setting. Lastly, we propose line-search variants for when Lipschitz parameters are unknown. Numerical experiments complement our theoretical results and demonstrate the practical efficacy of our methods.

title: VbotNav-0: Asynchronous Cloud-Edge Dual-Policy Navigation across Indoor and Outdoor Environments
summary: Continuous indoor-outdoor navigation connects destination-level reasoning with motion decisions that must respond to current observations. We present VbotNav-0, a cloud-edge dual-policy framework that links these processes through asynchronous policy-to-policy conditioning. The cloud policy produces subgoal guidance from visual history, navigation instructions, and route tokens; the edge policy combines available guidance with current RGB and LiDAR observations to generate local trajectories. This formulation allows the local perception-action loop to continue between cloud updates. A common route representation connects indoor paths and outdoor map routes, and the training recipe combines navigation demonstrations, corrective data, and grounded visual question answering (VQA). In the reported closed-loop evaluation of 258 episodes across 145 scenes, VbotNav-0 achieves 55.04% success rate and 55.03% success weighted by path length.

title: Safe Unicycle Navigation Among Multiple Obstacles Under Bounded Disturbances: A Learning-Augmented CLF-CBF Approach (Extended Version)
summary: This paper presents a robust control framework for safe navigation of a unicycle robot to a goal among multiple static obstacles under an unknown, time-varying disturbance. The controller solves a single real-time quadratic program (QP) that combines a goal-reaching term with one safety term per obstacle. The goal-reaching term is a cross-track control Lyapunov function built from body-frame tracking errors rather than a bearing angle, which keeps its Lie derivatives bounded everywhere, including the goal. Safety is encoded using robust control barrier functions, one per obstacle, each tightened by a closed-form, state-dependent disturbance bound. When stabilization and safety conflict, a slack variable relaxes only the convergence requirement, so that the safety constraints remain strictly enforced. Whenever the QP is feasible, the robust barrier constraints guarantee forward invariance of every obstacle's safe set under all admissible disturbances. Complementing this safety guarantee, a Lyapunov analysis yields an explicit ultimate bound on the distance to the goal. A learning-augmented variant replaces the fixed objective with a reinforcement-learning reference, which accelerates convergence when multiple constraints are simultaneously active. We further derive the obstacle separation below which the gap between two obstacles becomes too narrow to pass through under the robust constraints. For such gaps, a learned virtual goal for the Lyapunov function steers the robot around the obstacles without compromising safety. Simulations, a Monte Carlo study, and a comparison against a sampled-data robust baseline support the theoretical results.

title: Solution Set Dimensions in Convex Optimization and Primal-Polar Facial Signatures
summary: We study the possible dimensions of solution sets in linearly perturbed convex optimization problems and their behavior under convex duality. The dimensions of solution sets and inverse solution sets capture two complementary forms of nonuniqueness: that of optimal solutions for a given perturbation, and that of perturbations for which a given point is optimal. Although these two families are linked by Fenchel conjugacy, we show that their collections of dimensions can be prescribed independently for finite supercoercive convex functions. As a geometric consequence, we prove that the facial dimension signatures of a convex body and its polar can be prescribed independently. The connection between these two realization results is obtained by homogenizing the epigraphs of a function and its conjugate. In contrast, under simultaneous facial exposedness, we establish a dimensional obstruction relating the smallest positive proper face dimensions of the body and its polar. These results resolve two open questions posed by Roshchina and Tunçel.

title: Global Optimality of Pose Graph Optimization
summary: Pose Graph Optimization (PGO) is a classical and widely applied problem in state estimation for robotics, playing a fundamental role in localization, mapping, and navigation. Yet, it is nonconvex in nature and may have many local minimizers, thus difficult to analyze. In this paper, we investigate the optimization landscape and establish a sufficient condition of global optimality for PGO. The ultimate goal of this paper is to theoretically confirm that the optimization landscape is benign and attractive around the global minimizer, if noise is smaller than an explicit and a priori bound. To reveal such an insight, this paper develops three main technical results. First, we identify a proper basin of attraction (BOA) containing global minimizer, and characterize its geometric property by showing that its radius is controlled by noise in an explicit way. Then, by exploring the first order optimality conditions of PGO, we prove that a local minimizer is globally optimal if a noise-controlled criterion is satisfied. Finally, by combining above two results, we prove that one and only one local minimizer exists in the BOA and this minimizer is globally optimal, when the noise is smaller than an explicit bound that can be verified a priori. Numerical simulations validate the proposed theory under various random cases, showing that the obtained conditions provide an effective criterion for certifying the global optimality of PGO.

title: Enforcing a Strict Safety Margin in LLM Text Generation via Barrier Lyapunov Control
summary: Large language models are increasingly deployed without formal guarantees against toxic text generation. Existing control barrier function (CBF) based safety filters can keep the generation trajectory within a toxicity-free region, but do not enforce a positive distance from its boundary, allowing formally safe trajectories to approach the toxicity threshold arbitrarily closely and leaving little buffer against modelling errors or disturbances. We address this limitation with a Barrier Lyapunov Function (BLF) safety filter that enforces a prescribed clearance margin throughout generation while retaining the continuous-time transformer dynamics, including feedforward layers. The resulting safe input set is a half-space defined by a constraint affine in the control input, and is non-empty under certified surjectivity and classifier-nondegeneracy conditions. For margin-compatible initial conditions we prove that the clearance margin is never violated and that the prescribed clearance is restored exponentially, yielding an explicit clearance floor, and show that, as the margin vanishes, the admissible trajectories satisfy the exponential second-order CBF condition. We further derive an explicitly computable sufficient disturbance budget under which the clearance guarantee degrades gracefully. Simulations on a small transformer illustrate the resulting improvement in safety clearance.

title: Decision-Making in Digital Twins: Optimization, Control, and Learning
summary: A digital twin is a virtual representation of a physical system, continuously updated with data from the physical system, enabling dynamic information exchange and decision-making. This bidirectional interaction, which distinguishes digital twins from conventional simulation models, introduces new challenges to simulation-based optimization, control, and learning. This paper reviews recent developments in decision-making methodologies motivated by digital twins. We focus on three interconnected areas: simulation optimization, sequential decision making, and risk-aware decision making. For simulation optimization, we discuss data-driven simulation optimization under input uncertainty, streaming input data, decision-dependent observations, and limited computational and data-collection resources. For sequential decision making, we review the connections among digital twins, stochastic optimal control, and reinforcement learning, with emphasis on Bayesian approaches that update models and policies as new information becomes available. For risk-aware decision making, we discuss distributionally robust and Bayesian risk formulations as alternative approaches for addressing model uncertainty. Throughout the paper, we emphasize the common problem of making decisions while the underlying model is being updated. We conclude by identifying research challenges and opportunities.

title: Successful but Unsafe: An Analytical Benchmark for Revealing Collisions in Vision-and-Language Navigation
summary: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) agents are typically evaluated by whether they reach a target and how efficiently they follow an instructed route, yet these metrics provide little information about collision behavior. Moreover, continuous VLN evaluation commonly uses a sliding regime, where an agent can slide along obstacles after a collision, potentially masking the effect of unsafe actions on navigation performance. We introduce VLN-Safe, a benchmark for analyzing collision safety under two complementary evaluation regimes: sliding, reflecting common VLN evaluation practice, and blocking, where collision-inducing actions prevent forward motion and more directly expose their consequences. Across six published agents on R2R-CE, 38.5-56.8% of successful episodes contain contact under sliding, while switching to blocking decreases success rate by 11.7-36.1 percentage points. We further analyze signals for anticipating imminent collisions and find that depth geometry and recent movement history are more informative than policy-derived signals, while safe alternatives near the policy's preferred action are rarely available. Motivated by these findings, we introduce a training-free collision guard that vetoes risky forward actions, executes an escape maneuver, and returns control to the original policy. Under blocking, the guard reduces collision steps by 62-98% and improves success rate by 6.9-29.3 percentage points across five recurrent, topological, and vision-language-action agents. Under sliding, it leaves success rate unchanged while raising the share of collision-free successes by 4.1-12.4 points. These results reveal a substantial gap between task success and collision-safe navigation and show that lightweight collision-aware intervention can improve both safety and navigation performance.

title: Preliminary Exploration of Large Models Based on Self-Supervised Learning for Health Monitoring of Power Electronic Converters
comment: Accepted by Proceedings of the 2nd Electrical Artificial Intelligence Conference, EAIC 2025
summary: Current artificial intelligence (AI) methods for power electronics converters make limited use of the abundant unlabeled data generated during real-world operation. This underexplored resource holds significant potential for advancing model performance. To address this gap, this paper presents PE-TSFM, a time-series foundation model tailored for power module health monitoring. The model adopts the PatchTST architecture combined with self-supervised learning and is trained on more than 143 million timestamps, where over 98\% of this training data is unlabeled and collected directly from an operating traction converter. In degradation classification tasks, PE-TSFM achieves an accuracy of 87\%, considerably surpassing five conventional time-series AI models whose performance ranges from 27\% to 45\%. These results demonstrate the model's strong few-shot learning capability and generalization across different operating conditions. This work promotes a shift from narrowly focused models in power electronics toward unified, scalable foundation models that can unlock value from large-scale unlabeled operational data.

title: Matching Randomized Bounds for Finite-Sum Nonconvex-Concave Optimization
summary: We characterize the randomized component-oracle complexity of finite-sum nonconvex-concave optimization with a bounded dual domain. For $Φ(x)=\max_{y\in Y}n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x,y)$, the goal is to find an $\varepsilon$-stationary point of the Moreau envelope $Φ_{1/(2L)}$ with probability at least $2/3$ and a fixed query budget. Let $A=LΔ/\varepsilon^2$, $B=LD_Y/\varepsilon$, and $\bar B=\max\{1,B\}$, where $Δ$ bounds the initial primal gap and $D_Y$ bounds the dual diameter. For $A$ above a universal constant, the worst-case complexity is \[ \widetildeΘ\!\left(n+A\min\left\{ \sqrt n\,\bar B+\bar B^4,\ n^{3/4}\bar B\right\}\right). \] The bounds agree within constants for $B\le n^{1/4}$ and within one logarithm for larger $B$. Upper bounds require only mean-squared averaged smoothness and concavity of the average in the dual variable; lower bounds already hold under individual smoothness. The lower constructions cover adaptive component selection, arbitrary query norms, private randomization, and outputs that were never queried. A cone construction gives the small-diameter bound, while a serial branch construction and balanced replication give the remaining two regimes. On the upper side, a persistent estimator with primal averaging complements accelerated proximal dual steps equipped with an explicit primal certificate. The characterization takes the worst case over admissible known dual domains and finite dimensions.

title: DexCast: Learning Real-World Dexterous Control from Human Videos
summary: Recent advances in 3D hand-object interaction (HOI) perception have opened new opportunities for learning dexterous robotic skills from human videos. However, existing dexterous imitation learning methods often rely on costly and manually teleoperated robot demonstrations, requiring substantial human effort. Therefore, we build DEXCAST, a framework that learns dexterous robotic hand control directly from monocular RGB-D videos by leveraging joint HOI reconstructions, without requiring any teleoperation. Furthermore, how to model high-dimensional robotic hand motion and extract temporal context to inform future action generation remains a key challenge. To this end, we propose a DexHand Motion Perception Module (DMPM) to capture inter-joint coordination and temporal dependencies in compact latent representations that condition our diffusion policy. Extensive real-world experiments demonstrate that DEXCAST achieves exceptional performance across diverse dexterous manipulation tasks.

title: Generic Local Identifiability Does Not Imply Generic Global Identifiability in Linear Networks
summary: We give a counterexample to the implication from generic local to generic global identifiability for linear networks with a fixed topology, independently unknown edge coefficients, and selected excited and measured nodes. A six-node network with nine unknown coefficients has exactly two compatible parameter vectors generically. Adding six excited and measured nodes preserves this ambiguity while making the added coefficients directly recoverable. The resulting twelve-node structure has forty-two independent unknown coefficients and zero diagonal. For every positive bound on the largest eigenvalue magnitude, a nonempty open set of parameters has two distinct compatible networks satisfying that bound. This holds for both real and complex coefficients. Other open regions have exactly one admissible solution. The proof uses a rational transformation exchanging the two solutions and a common limiting matrix whose fourth power vanishes. Exact rational-number certificates verify an explicit pair. The construction also extends algebraically when the unknown coordinates are whole rational transfer functions. Genericity in prescribed numerator and denominator coefficient families, and the requirement that every transfer function vanish at infinite frequency, remain separate questions.
